title: Deskcity 0.2.0
changes: Safer defaults: refusal pass-off (a refused job handed to another model) is off on a fresh install, turning it on needs your dashboard password, and it stops after one hop.
The installer asks whether to set a dashboard password, with Yes as the default. Unattended installs (--yes) skip it and print a clear warning until you run npm run set-password.
Drop-in add-ons: a folder under addons/ adds its own pages and routes. Each one is off until you switch it on, and one kill switch turns them all off.
Browser automation is now the optional addons/browser add-on, so a plain install is smaller. npm run addons:install installs the add-ons you use, and npm run update does it for you.
The agents API has its own address, /api/agents. The old /api/pipeline/agents address still works for now and says where it moved.
DESKCITY_JOBS_DISABLED=1 stops the background jobs, but the nightly backup keeps running. The old name PIPELINE_DISABLED=1 still works.
An approval line: costly jobs and sessions the hub starts on its own wait for your OK.

When a job fails because a worker couldn't reach something (permission denied, needs a sign-in), the hub files one question for you naming the worker and the reason, instead of failing quietly. Retry is still the button under Problems.
Questions with choices get one button per choice.
A busy desk can pass new jobs to a helper desk (off unless you set it).
Half-price switches for hub-run desks (prompt caching and batch), off until you turn them on.
Jobs ride out a short network drop instead of failing.
Long hand-offs arrive whole, or are refused with a reason.
Campus: a city fund from the store tax that the board votes on, a City fund panel, and votes that show in Waiting for you. Workers can found their own districts by a vote. All play money.

City life on the campus: a menu with a switch per effect. Power lines show how close workers are to their caps, cones mark stuck buildings, vans carry hand-offs in 3D, busy buildings stay lit after hours, workers walk in each morning, a sunbeam follows your pet and idle workers sit in a diner. All from what the campus already knows, no AI cost.

City life, part 2: shipping docks, a cargo barge, a library that shows the last backup, tubes that carry what is waiting for you, a crane over projects with recent reviews, balloon banners for spend and alerts, a blimp with the newest changes, and weather routines (umbrellas in rain, fewer people out in snow, the pet naps indoors). They read one small new address that returns counts only.
A campus casino where workers can play a slot game you add with their play credits. Off until you turn it on, never real money and no AI calls.
The 3D campus re-checks its quality setting when the graphics chip changes, and Waiting and In progress cards no longer shrink to a thin line.
Fixes from a full security and code review: sign-in, hand-offs, restore, the updater and the Admin page.
README and user guide: what caps cover (hard caps stop the paid jobs the hub runs itself; coding agents that run outside the hub report their own cost estimates), and how add-ons work.
For contributors: npm run lint and npm run typecheck, which CI runs first.

title: Deskcity 0.1.0: first release
changes: One local hub for every AI worker you use: Claude, Gemini, OpenAI-style and local models, and coding agents such as Claude Code.
Give a job and pick who takes it next, on another model. Each step's model, tokens and cost are in the AI call log, and a finished job can be replayed step by step.
A monthly cap per worker, a score from 0 to 100 on every finished job, and one list, Waiting for you, for hires, questions and money warnings.
Four views of the same hub: 2D city, 3D city, Neural and plain pages.
AI helpers are off until you turn them on. Spending needs your dashboard password once you set one.
Nightly backups with a restore test, and updates that keep your data: npm run update.
Install on Windows by double-clicking install.cmd (Mac or Linux: bash install.sh), then start it with start.cmd (or bash start.sh).
New here? Run npm run demo to look around with no keys, or open this folder in Claude Code and say: set up my hub.
This was the first public kit.
It was cut from a month of private development.
